items.q: Well, we played ghetto, mandolin, and Sylvester, he was on my daddy's bass. Well, we used to go out around the lakefront.

ctx.x: Does that have anything to do with strength? No, it doesn't.

items.title: Crescent City Crystals: Dave Bailey, Harold Christophe, Albert Delone, Sylvester Handy Interview, 1963-11-13
items.q: Sylvester Handy, Julius Handy, and John Handy. You got them all into one family. We had a string instrument.

ctx.x: Born in New Orleans and the Trimmy.

Trimmy? Oh, I know. From Trimmy to the Rocky Green. Like London Avenue. 7-Watt, you know? What... Who taught you to play guitar? Now, who taught me how to play guitar? My father played guitar, you see? Yeah. But my first instrument, I used to pick up his guitar. Uh-huh. And all that harmony was right in my head. Yeah.
